sections.name: Applicant Information & Operation Details
criteria: Overview of the Business: The extent to which the applicant provides relevant context about their farm or agricultural operation, including the scale, type of operation, and any existing infrastructure. The extent to which the applicant demonstrates that the operation is actively engaged in commercial agricultural production, including the scale of production, markets served, and the roll that agricultural production plays in the overall business or organizational model.

Organizational Alignment: The extent to which the applicant describes how the project aligns with their business goals and addresses specific operational challenges, including region-specific challenges.
Previous Grant Funding: The applicant’s history of receiving and utilizing grant funding will be considered, ensuring they have the capacity to manage project funds effectively.
sections.template:
{name} is a commercial greenhouse operation in {town}. The growing space covers {sqft} square feet under a covering of {covering}, and the site is served by the utility {utility}. Our area sees about {hdd} heating degree days a year, so the greenhouse must be heated for much of the growing season. We estimate our annual heating cost at {estimate_point} dollars, within a range of {estimate_low} to {estimate_high} dollars.

The operation is actively engaged in commercial agricultural production. We grow {UNKNOWN: crops grown and annual production volume} and sell to {UNKNOWN: markets served}. Greenhouse production accounts for {UNKNOWN: share of farm income from greenhouse production} of the business and is central to how the farm earns its income. The farm has been in continuous operation for {UNKNOWN: years in continuous operation}.

This project fits our business goals because heating fuel is one of our largest operating costs. Long, cold winters in our region make heat loss through the greenhouse covering a direct operational challenge, and reducing that loss is the most practical way to protect our margins and keep growing through the cold months.

Previous grant funding: {UNKNOWN: previous grant awards received and how they were used}. We will manage project funds through the farm's existing bookkeeping, keeping every invoice and payment record for the project.

sections.name: Project Details
criteria: Project Description: The extent to which the project is clearly defined. This should address the issue being solved, the proposed solution, and why the applicant chose this specific project.

Project Goals: The clarity and specificity of the project short-term objectives and goals. The project should outline how it will improve farm sustainability, reduce costs, mitigate climate change, and/or address food safety or energy use in measurable ways. The goals should focus on what the project aims to achieve during or shortly after completion.

Impacts: The measurable short-term outcomes, which should focus on quantifiable changes in environmental, operational, and financial performance. Impacts reflect the actual results achieved from implementing the project goals.
sections.template:
The problem we are solving is heat loss. {name} spends an estimated {estimate_point} dollars a year on heating, and much of that heat escapes through the {covering} covering on cold nights. The proposed solution is {top_fix_name}. We chose this project because, of the energy-saving measures assessed for our greenhouse, it offers the largest annual saving, and it can be installed in the existing structure without interrupting production.

Our short-term goals are to install {top_fix_name} across the {sqft} square feet of growing space, to cut heating fuel use from the first heating season after installation, and to lower our operating costs so the farm stays profitable. Burning less fuel also helps mitigate climate change by cutting the greenhouse gas emissions of the operation.

We expect these measurable impacts once the project is complete: heating cost savings of {top_fix_saves_usd} dollars a year, about {gallons_saved} fewer gallons of heating fuel burned each year, and about {carbon_tons_saved} fewer metric tons of carbon dioxide emitted each year. With a project cost of {top_fix_cost_usd} dollars, the measure pays for itself in about {top_fix_payback_years} years. We will compare fuel deliveries and heating bills before and after installation to confirm these results.

sections.name: Feasibility of the Project Plan
criteria: Timeline: A clear, achievable timeline that outlines milestones, project phases, and completion dates.
Team Members: The qualifications, roles, and responsibilities of the team members. This should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to execute the project effectively.
Permits & Regulatory Compliance: Evaluation of the applicant’s ability to secure necessary permits and approvals, ensuring compliance with all relevant federal, state, or local regulations.
Budget: The completeness and accuracy of the budget, including clarity on how the project funds will be allocated.
sections.template:
Timeline: We will order {top_fix_name} as soon as a contract is in place, and no work will begin before then. Installation is planned for {UNKNOWN: planned installation dates and milestones}, and the project will be complete and operating before the completion deadline of {UNKNOWN: project completion deadline}. The project phases are ordering materials, installation, and a performance check during the following heating season.

Team members: {UNKNOWN: names, qualifications, roles and responsibilities of the project team and installer}. The owner of {name} will manage the project, oversee installation and keep all project records.

Permits and regulatory compliance: We will secure {UNKNOWN: permits and approvals required for this project} from the town of {town} and any other relevant authority before installation begins, and the project will comply with all applicable federal, state and local regulations.

Budget: The total project cost is {top_fix_cost_usd} dollars. We request {grant_request} dollars in grant funds, and the farm will pay the remaining {farmer_match} dollars as a cash match, meeting the required cost share of {UNKNOWN: required cost-share percentage}. All project funds will go to the purchase and installation of {top_fix_name}, as shown in the fixes and budget table.

sections.name: Sustainability & Long-Term Impacts
criteria: Sustainability: How the project contributes to long-term sustainability of the agricultural operation, including energy efficiency, promoting environmental stewardship, and supporting farm profitability. This includes the proposed project’s durability and ability to maintain the positive effects over time.

Metrics to Track Impacts: The applicant should define how they will measure the long-term impacts of the project. Metrics should track continued success and the enduring benefits of the project, including impacts on environmental performance, energy use, water use, production efficiency, and food safety over time.
Post-Project Sustainability: A clear plan for maintaining the project’s success after completion, ensuring that the impact is sustained beyond the grant period.
Warranties and Guarantees: The inclusion of product warranties, service guarantees, or any other long-term support for the project.

Operation & Maintenance: The applicant’s ability to maintain the project after completion. This includes ongoing operation, maintenance, and ensuring that the system remains functional and effective in the long term.
sections.template:
Sustainability: {top_fix_name} is a durable capital improvement that will keep reducing heat loss from the greenhouse for many years. By saving about {top_fix_saves_usd} dollars a year in heating costs, it supports the long-term profitability of {name}. By burning about {gallons_saved} fewer gallons of fuel each year, the farm will emit about {carbon_tons_saved} fewer metric tons of carbon dioxide annually, a lasting contribution to environmental stewardship.

Metrics to track impacts: We will record heating fuel deliveries and heating bills every season and compare them with our estimated pre-project heating cost of {estimate_point} dollars a year, adjusting for winter severity with heating degree days for {town}. We will also log greenhouse temperatures and crop output, so we can show that energy use has fallen while production efficiency has been maintained.

Post-project sustainability: The measure pays back its full cost in about {top_fix_payback_years} years, so its savings keep benefiting the farm well beyond the grant period.

Warranties and guarantees: {UNKNOWN: product warranty and installer service guarantee terms}.

Operation and maintenance: Farm staff will inspect {top_fix_name} before each heating season, repair any damage promptly and operate it as designed, so the system remains functional and effective in the long term.

sections.name: Project Financing & Support Documents
criteria: Demonstration of Financing: How the applicant will finance the project upfront and manage the required match. The applicant should demonstrate the ability to cover the remaining project costs and how the match requirement will be met. This includes any financial documentation such as bank reference letters, executed loans, or grant funds from other sources.

Priority will be given to applications where farm-generated revenue is a primary source of operational income and where the proposed project meaningfully supports the continued viability of agricultural production.
Support Documents: The completeness of all required supporting documentation, including any financial references, quotes from vendors or contractors, and proof of available financing.
sections.template:
Demonstration of financing: The total cost of {top_fix_name} is {top_fix_cost_usd} dollars. We are requesting {grant_request} dollars from {UNKNOWN: grant program name}, and {name} will pay the remaining {farmer_match} dollars as a cash match from farm revenue, which meets the minimum cash match of {UNKNOWN: required cash match percentage}. Because the grant is paid as a reimbursement, the farm will pay the full project cost upfront using {UNKNOWN: source of upfront financing, such as farm savings, a line of credit or an executed loan} and will be reimbursed for the grant share after installation. We will provide {UNKNOWN: bank reference letter, line of credit letter or other financial documentation} to show that the farm can cover these costs.

Farm-generated revenue is a primary source of our operating income, with greenhouse sales making up {UNKNOWN: share of operating income from farm-generated revenue}. This project supports the continued viability of that production by lowering our largest seasonal operating cost.

Support documents: The application includes the budget for this project area, {UNKNOWN: list of supporting documents attached}, and the proof of available financing described above.
